hypotheses.subject: 9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e
hypotheses.summary: The deploy of revision 9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e at 15:13Z introduced a latency regression: p95 began climbing in the very next minute (220ms -> 900ms -> 1800ms -> 5000ms) and errors rose to 12% as requests began timing out. It is the only recorded change to io-shop in the preceding month.

supporting_evidence.claim: Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-08-16T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-16T15:13:00Z contains only this one deploy - no other change, and no feature-flag toggle, is recorded in the month before onset.
WARN io-shop: p95 latency at 1800ms, up from a 220ms baseline
bucket 2026-09-16T15:13:00Z error_rate 0.01 / p95 220 (last healthy minute, same minute as the deploy) then 15:14 p95 900, 15:15 p95 1800, 15:16 p95 5000 with error_rate 0.12

hypotheses.summary: Alternatively the degradation was not caused by any recorded change to io-shop - e.g. a slow or saturated downstream dependency or resource exhaustion - and the 15:13 deploy is coincidental. The logs show only generic latency/timeout symptoms with no stack traces, error codes or dependency names, so this cannot be excluded. To distinguish it I would have needed dependency-level latency metrics or logs naming the slow call, or the effect of a rollback.
